item.title: DB Jay Timmons' status downgraded for Ohio State vs USC
item.description: Ohio State defensive back Jay Timmons has been downgraded to doubtful for the USC game on Oct. 31. Timmons was one of two starters listed as questionable in the Buckeyes ' initial availability report, alongside wide receiver Brandon Inniss , whose status remains the same. None of the injuries are specified in the reports, which are released by the Big Ten. Timmons made his first appearance in two games against Indiana on Oct. 17 , recording seven tackles, two pass breakups and a forced fumble. But the freshman was pulled from the lineup once again and missed Ohio State's final defensive drives due to an apparent injury. Freshman wide receiver Brock Boyd became one of 10 Buckeyes ruled out in the previous availability report from Oct. 29. Veteran quarterback Julian Sayin and running back Ja'Kobi Jackson are the only starters unavailable against the Trojans . Sayin is out "indefinitely" with an undisclosed injury he suffered in the fourth quarter of the Indiana game, and Jackson underwent foot surgery, according to a report from ESPN on Oct. 21. bmackay@dispatch.com @brimackay15 This article originally appeared on The Columbus Dispatch: DB Jay Timmons' status downgraded for Ohio State vs USC

The elder Ilicevic enjoyed a lengthy career in German football and played a particularly important role in helping Hamburg preserve their Bundesliga status during one of the club’s most dramatic relegation battles. For Niko, Sunday’s encounter could therefore represent both a historic personal achievement and an unusual continuation of his family’s Bundesliga story. Uncle Ivo Ilicevic’s distinguished career in German football The family connection to HSV adds considerable historical significance to Sunday’s possible debut. Born in Aschaffenburg in November 1986, Niko’s uncle Ivo enjoyed a lengthy professional career in German football, representing six Bundesliga and 2. Bundesliga clubs across a journey that began in the lower divisions and eventually took him onto the international stage with Croatia. Ilicevic developed in the youth ranks of local club Viktoria Aschaffenburg before moving to SV Darmstadt 98. The technically gifted attacking midfielder began establishing himself in senior football with the Lilies. His performances attracted the attention of VfL Bochum, who brought him to the Bundesliga in the summer of 2006. A subsequent loan spell at SpVgg Greuther Fürth offered Ilicevic greater opportunities to demonstrate his attacking qualities. The move proved an important developmental step, with the midfielder registering four goals in 38 second-division appearances before joining 1. FC Kaiserslautern in the summer of 2009. It was in the Pfalz that Ilicevic truly established himself as an influential figure in German professional football. Under head coach Marco Kurz, Kaiserslautern assembled one of the strongest teams in the 2009/10 2. Bundesliga campaign. Ilicevic contributed four goals in 30 league appearances as the Red Devils secured the second-division championship and returned to Germany’s top flight after four seasons away. The following campaign represented another significant milestone. Kaiserslautern surprised many observers by finishing seventh in the Bundesliga, with Ilicevic contributing five league goals in 21 appearances. The midfielder also received recognition at international level, earning senior appearances for Croatia. His performances eventually attracted the attention of Hamburger SV, who secured his services at the end of the summer 2011 transfer window. Ilicevic subsequently spent five seasons at the Volksparkstadion, becoming part of an HSV side that experienced frequent managerial changes, fluctuating performances, and repeated battles to preserve its Bundesliga status. By the time his five-year association with HSV ended in 2016, Ilicevic had accumulated 84 Bundesliga appearances for the Hanseatic club, scoring ten league goals. His career subsequently continued abroad with Anzhi Makhachkala in Russia and Kairat Almaty in Kazakhstan. A brief return to Germany followed in 2019, when the veteran attacker joined 1. FC Nürnberg and made three further Bundesliga appearances before leaving the club that summer. Ivo Ilicevic helped preserve Hamburg’s Bundesliga status For all the different chapters of his career, one of Ilicevic’s most consequential moments in German football came during HSV’s extraordinary 2015 relegation battle. Hamburg had spent every season in the Bundesliga since the competition’s foundation in 1963. That distinction was under serious threat after Bruno Labbadia’s side finished the 2014/15 campaign in 16th place, forcing a two-legged relegation playoff against Karlsruher SC. In the 73rd minute, the Croatian international scored the equalizer that rescued a 1-1 draw for Hamburg and prevented Karlsruhe from taking a first-leg advantage into the return fixture. Four days later, the two teams met again at Karlsruhe’s Wildparkstadion. A 2-1 Hamburg victory preserved the club’s Bundesliga status for another season. Ilicevic had played his part in setting up that escape. The Croatian eventually departed in 2016, two years before HSV suffered its first Bundesliga relegation in 2018. Now, more than a decade after his uncle helped Hamburg preserve its place in Germany’s top flight, Niko Ilicevic stands on the threshold of beginning his own Bundesliga career against the very same club. Adi Hütter praises Frankfurt’s exceptional young talent Hütter confirmed at the Friday pre-match press conference that the attacking midfielder would be included in Frankfurt’s plans for Sunday’s Bundesliga meeting with HSV. The Austrian coach spoke enthusiastically about Ilicevic’s development, while emphasizing the importance of managing the youngster’s introduction to professional football. “He won’t have much time to celebrate because, in all likelihood, he’ll be in the squad,” Hütter explained. “To be part of a Bundesliga squad at 16 years of age is already extraordinary.” “He was part of the training camp and has developed tremendously over the past few months,” Hütter continued. “He’s an exceptional footballer with the ball, but he’s also learned to stand his ground and win challenges.” Ilicevic first attracted widespread attention in May 2025 when he participated in Frankfurt’s senior training sessions at just 14 years of age. The German-Croatian youngster has subsequently continued his development in Frankfurt’s youth ranks, registering four goals and three assists in seven appearances for the club’s U19 side this season. “If I feel that it isn’t the right moment, I won’t do it,” the Frankfurt trainer explained. “The time will come. He’ll play eventually, and then he’ll simply be 16 years and a few weeks old.” GGFN | Peter Weis

item.description: Max Verstappen has won two races so far in 2026 [Reuters] Max Verstappen accused Racing Bulls driver Liam Lawson of "not very smart behaviour" after the two collided in Friday practice at the Mexico City Grand Prix. The four-time champion said Lawson had tried to "drive me off the track at the hairpin" during the second session. Ferrari's Charles Leclerc headed McLaren's Lando Norris in the times. Mercedes driver Kimi Antonelli, who is poised to clinch his first world title on Sunday, was fourth fastest behind team-mate George Russell. Verstappen and Lawson clashed in the stadium section towards the end of the lap, with the two cars hitting each other side on after running through three corners side by side. "Maybe not very smart behaviour what he was trying to do there," said Verstappen. "At the end of the day it is not going to change my weekend, but if I were him I would act a little smarter - and when you're fighting for your seat it's not very smart behaviour." Lawson is one of three drivers competing for two seats at Racing Bulls, Red Bull's junior team, next year, alongside current team-mate Arvid Lindblad and Bulgarian Formula 2 front-runner Nikola Tsolov. Verstappen has an influential position within the Red Bull organisation as their star driver. The Dutchman added: "When he saw me coming, he suddenly started to accelerate. I don't know what was going through his head, that he wanted to drive me off the track in the hairpin. "That's not very sensible behaviour from someone in his position, to pick a fight with me." item.title: Houston Rockets open NBA Cup play against Dallas but more focused on managing injuries
item.description: Houston Rockets guard Fred VanVleet was set to play against the Mavericks on Friday but would likely miss Saturday's game against Oklahoma City. (Elizabeth Conley/Houston Chronicle) DALLAS - The Houston Rockets play their first NBA Cup game Friday night against the Dallas Mavericks at American Airlines Center. The Rockets are in Group A along with the Mavericks, Denver Nuggets, Phoenix Suns and Utah Jazz. Each team will play a game against the other teams in their group. The top team in each of the six groups and two wild cards (the best second-place team in each conference) will advance to the knockout rounds. Coach Ime Udoka said the in-season tournament offers "added incentive," but more than anything, he wants his 5-0 team to continue playing good basketball. "It adds some to it, and we know there's a goal at the end of the line on this, but we're playing good and we want to continue that regardless," he said. Houston has qualified for the knockout round once in Udoka's tenure. The Rockets made the semifinal in his second season before losing to the eventual champion Oklahoma City Thunder. The Rockets will have starting point guard Fred VanVleet against Dallas. The veteran, coming off a torn ACL, is only playing in one half of Houston's back-to-backs, meaning he will almost certainly miss the Rockets' Saturday night matchup with the Oklahoma City Thunder at Toyota Center. Udoka said that if the Rockets were fully healthy, he'd likely look to stagger VanVleet and Steven Adams on either half of back-to-backs depending on matchups. However, Houston isn't healthy - Adams is out with a right calf strain, starting center Alperen Şengün and Reed Sheppard are out with lower back soreness. Marcus Smart, who was questionable with a left forearm strain, will play against Dallas. Udoka said the uncertainty of Smart's and Sheppard's availability was the primary reason he chose to play VanVleet against the Mavericks. Last year's NBA Cup champion, the New York Knicks, were initially not going to raise a banner for their victory but decided to do so after winning the NBA Finals. Udoka, asked his preference on raising a banner if Houston won the NBA Cup, kept it simple. "I don't care." Rockets pick up Reed Sheppard's contract option The Rockets announced Friday that they picked up the fourth-year option for Sheppard, an expected move that keeps the No. 3 pick in the 2024 draft under contract through the 2027-28 season. Sheppard played all 82 games last season, starting 21 games and averaging 13.5 points, 3.4 assists and 1.5 steals per game. The guard becomes eligible for an extension this offseason. Coach Ben Johnson’s Chicago Bears made a huge move to acquire a massive man, defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons, that has him daydreaming about prime-time games . The Bears have become a trendy Super Bowl pick, led by QB Caleb Williams and his ‘Scottie Pippen’ sidekick in the receiver room . Following the trade, Stephen A. Smith of ESPN shared his take on what the Bears must do now that they’ve added Simmons to a defense that has a chance to get a lot better in a short timeframe. “I’ve been bullish on the Chicago Bears because of Caleb Williams from last year, I believe in this brother, and I believe in what they’re doing right now. Because this is where this all changes, a move like this, understand the magnitude of it, for Simmons, the Chicago Bears gave up two first-round picks, that’s a lot in the NFL. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “But he’s (Simmons) worth it, we all know what he brings to the table, they’re also inheriting his lucrative contract, we have to take that into consideration as well. This message is the Chicago Bears sayin’, we’re going all in, we’re trying to win it all right now.” Smith noted that Williams is still on his rookie deal, which necessitated them pushing their chips to the center of the table to chase a Super Bowl. Bears GM Ryan Poles echoed Smith’s notion, sharing his thoughts on Simmons and their Super Bowl aspirations . The Bears’ D’Andre Swift-led running game also could play a huge role, as teams load up to stop Williams. Swift had 78 yards and a touchdown in a huge performance against the Patriots that sparked championship dreams. The Bears have a lot of hurdles to jump before qualifying for the big game, but for now, they are looking like a strong choice to make a deep playoff run. item.title: Cardinals HC Mike LaFluer Gives Positive Carson Beck Injury Update Heading into Week 8
item.description: TEMPE, ARIZONA - MAY 08: Carson Beck #19 of the Arizona Cardinals practices in team rookie mincamp at Dignity Health Arizona Cardinals Training Center on May 08, 2026 in Tempe, Arizona. (Photo by Christian Petersen/Getty Images) Getty GLENDALE, ARIZONA - AUGUST 22: Carson Beck #19 of the Arizona Cardinals walks on the field prior to a preseason game against the Dallas Cowboys at State Farm Stadium on August 22, 2026 in Glendale, Arizona. Cowboys won 34-13. (Photo by Norm Hall/Getty Images) Getty Carson Beck's comeback coming soon? Getty The latest updates out of Glendale signal that Carson Beck’s return could be right around the corner. Beck rejoined the team for Wednesday’s session, and the rookie is already making an impression. The Arizona Cardinals are taking a cautious approach by keeping him on a limited workload, but Beck’s deep-throw ability in drills is already raising eyebrows. Mike LaFleur Gives Carson Beck Update Getty Carson Beck starts practice. Addressing the media on Friday, Cardinals HC Mike LaFleur detailed the progress Beck has made during his first week back at practice. “He’s done a good job, LaFleur said, per Dana Scott . “Last week was kind of a setback because of nothing other than some unfortunate circumstances in the back. But when he gets out there, he practices with a purpose, practices to get better just like all these guys do.” Before getting Beck suited up for live practices, they put him through a separate workout on Tuesday, the team’s day off, to see how he moves in the pocket after Beck dealt with back spasms last week, according to Josh Weinfuss . The workout will determine how much, and if at all, Beck practices this week. LaFleur said Beck’s back flared up on him. Should the Cardinals Rush Carson Beck? Getty Carson Beck’s comeback coming soon? However, LaFleur wanted to set the record straight right away, so he clarified that Beck will be limited for now during his Wednesday media appearance. “He’s limited as well,” LaFleur said in his Wednesday press conference . “Threw it well yesterday. I guess we’ll kind of see today in 11-on-11 action.” What makes this situation so compelling is that Carson Beck was always expected to return at some point this season. It was strictly a matter of how fast his body responded. The Cardinals are dropping games, and the urgency to throw the rookie back out there grows by the week. While this feels like the ideal window for Beck to bounce back from his rib injury, LaFleur slammed the door on any immediate QB controversy by confirming Jacoby Brissett will start this Sunday. Arizona is refusing to rush their young signal-caller, but holding out until their late Week 14 bye might prove fatal for a season that is slipping away. item.title: Cowboys’ Jerry Jones Sends Confusing Message on Struggling Starter
item.description: DaRon Bland #26 of the Dallas Cowboys Getty If there is one area that the Dallas Cowboys have obviously needed to clean up, even going back to training camp, it has been the cornerback situation. The team’s plan this year appeared to be based mostly on hope, that is, the hope that DaRon Bland could recapture the form that led him to nine interceptions and an All-Pro selection back in 2023, as well as the hope that a healthy Shavon Revel, who spent much of last year recovering from an ACL surgery and a subsequent setback, would prove worthy of the third-round pick the Cowboys used on him in 2025. It was a thin plan all along, and the Cowboys only added Cobie Durant as their lone new corner in the room. A quick check on how it’s going: take Pro Football Focus grades however you will, but as of Week 8, Bland is rated as the 88th corner in the league, out of 97, and Revel is No. 92 of 97. Durant has been out with a hamstring injury since Week 2. DaRon Bland in $90 Million Contract The Cowboys deserve credit for acting aggressively when an opportunity presented itself, trading for Joey Porter Jr. from the Steelers earlier this month. Porter has shown himself to be a shutdown corner thus far, but the problem for the Steelers remains that the rest of the room is still based on the hope that Bland can bounce back on the opposite boundary. On Friday, team owner Jerry Jones was asked during his appearance on 105.3 The Fan in Dallas what he thought of Bland’s underwhelming performance this season. item.title: Mbappé missed out on the Ballon D’Or by 28 points
item.description: Real Madrid's Spanish forward #10 Kylian Mbappe talks to Spain and Barcelona midfielder Rodri and England and Bayern Munich forward Harry Kane (L) during the 2026 Ballon d'Or France Football award ceremony at the Palladium Theatre in London on October 26, 2026. (Photo by FRANCK FIFE / AFP via Getty Images) | AFP via Getty Images Kylian Mbappé fell short in the 2026 Ballon d’Or race by just 28 points, with the full voting breakdown revealing how close the Real Madrid forward came to beating Harry Kane. Kane collected 1,055 points to Mbappé’s 1,027, making this the fourth-closest finish between the leading two candidates in the award’s history. Barcelona’s Lamine Yamal finished third with 881 points. The Bayern Munich striker received 40 first-place votes, compared with 23 for Mbappé. That stronger backing at the top of the ballots helped Kane secure the trophy, despite the narrow gap in their overall totals. For Madrid, Mbappé was comfortably their highest-ranked player. Jude Bellingham finished 11th with 107 points, missing out on the top 10, while Vinícius Júnior placed 17th on 26 points. Marc Cucurella followed in 18th with 16 points. Rodri took fourth place with 726 points, ahead of Lionel Messi on 612. Paris Saint-Germain pair Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Ousmane Dembélé finished sixth and seventh respectively. The figures put a number on Mbappé’s disappointment. He had been among the favourites heading into the ceremony, but ultimately finished within touching distance of the prize as Kane became the first English player to win it since Michael Owen’s success back in 2001.

item.title: Islam Makhachev Hints At UFC Retirement In The Near Future
item.description: Islam Makhachev will not be back in action until mid-2027 and when he does return the UFC welterweight champion will only have a few fights left. Many expected Makhachev to defend his UFC welterweight title against knockout ace Carlos Prates at UFC 336 this coming January, but the pound-for-pound king simply wasn’t going to be ready. With Makhachev sidelined for the time being, UFC matchmakers booked an interim title fight between Prates and fellow top contender Michael Morales to co-headline UFC 336. The winner is expected to unify the belt with Makhachev some time after Ramadan. Makhachev, who has only fought four times over the past three years, is eager to see who the more deserving contender is between Prates and Morales . Of course, that may not be the only reason why Makhachev postponed his UFC 336 title defense. The UFC superstar could be nursing an injury or simply buying his time to play out the final few fights of his storied career. The latter seems more likely given Makhachev’s social media post on Friday. The UFC champion confirmed his next fight is “one of the last in my career,” meaning he aims to make it count. Fighting Prates in January would have been a solid choice to do just that, but Makhachev has earned the right to wait if he wants to. Just don’t expect Makhachev to fight too many times after his next walk to the Octagon. My next fight is one of the last in my career. They say Prates is too dangerous for me and Morales is too good for me. Now, they face a hobbled Mississippi State Bulldogs team floundering after the loss of quarterback Kamario Taylor, one of the brightest stars of the early season. The Bulldogs flew to a 4-0 record largely thanks to Taylor’s offensive prowess, but have dropped three straight contests by a combined 110-38. Jeff Lebby’s offense has struggled without its elite trigger man, teams have contained dynamic running back Fluff Bothwell, while the defense hasn’t kept opponents out of the end zone with any consistency. Teams have had their way with the Mississippi State defense, giving up an average of 267 yards through the air and 124 on the ground. In the lopsided loss to the Crimson Tide, the Bulldogs allowed 179 rushing yards and four touchdowns, while the Sooners rushed for 184 — eclipsing 85 yards for the first time since the start of conference play. item.title: Judge orders MHSAA to reinstate Grand Rapids CC in football playoffs
item.description: A judge ruled in favor of Grand Rapids Catholic Central on Friday, Oct. 30, ordering the Michigan High School Athletic Association to reinstate the Cougars in the Division 5 football playoffs, according to a statement from the MHSAA. "The MHSAA’s difficult decision to remove Grand Rapids Catholic Central from the football playoffs for having fielded an ineligible player this season was challenged today in state court, which entered an order directing Catholic Central’s first-round participation in the playoffs," the state high school association said in a statement emailed to the Free Press. The Cougars were set to host Comstock Park (4-5) at 7 p.m. Friday, with the winner advancing to the district final next week to await the winner of Berrien Springs vs. Lakewood. FOLLOW ALONG: Michigan high school football playoffs: Live scores from MHSAA first round On Thursday, the MHSAA announced it had removed Grand Rapids Catholic Central from the postseason for the use of an ineligible player over six games during the regular season, which forced the GRCC to forfeit five regular-season victories. With the forfeits, Grand Rapids Catholic Central no longer qualified for the state playoffs in the MHSAA's playoff-point system. In the statement, the MHSAA said it "was not provided an opportunity to participate in those legal proceedings and only learned of the court’s order late this afternoon." The MHSAA would have presented new evidence, received in the past week, that explains its decision, the group added in its statement. According to Kent County court records , there is a show-cause hearing scheduled for Friday, Nov. 6 at 9 a.m. [ Sign up for our new Michigan Sidelines statewide high school sports newsletter ] According to Catholic Central, the ineligible player enrolled in the school in January 2026, and the MHSAA sent a letter in August confirming their eligibility. In October, the MHSAA informed CC it had new information about the family's former residence and renewed its investigation. CC held the player out of the final two games. The MHSAA ruled, one day before the 2026 playoffs were set to begin, that the player did not satisfy the "full and complete" residence change as required by the state handbook. "While the MHSAA disagrees with the court’s order and handling of the matter, we respect the legal process and believe the courts will appreciate hearing from us on this important matter,” the group also said in its statement following Friday's court decision. item.title: Travis Hunter Makes Strong Statement on Deion Sanders Amid Colorado Struggles
item.description: Travis Hunter brushes off any controversy about CB rotation. Getty In his fourth season as the head coach of the Colorado Buffaloes, it’s been a rocky year for Deion Sanders. Colorado is 2-5 overall, has lost five games in a row and sits in last place in the Big 12 at 0-4 in conference play. As questions continue to circle about Sanders’ future in Boulder and whether he can turn things around, his former star player Travis Hunter had nothing but great things to say about him during a recent appearance on Ja’Marr Chase’s podcast, Chasing No. 1. Hunter Makes Strong Statement on Sanders Looking back at his college recruitment, Hunter said he was set on going to Florida State until he got in touch with Sanders. “I was 100% going to Florida State,” Hunter said. Sanders ultimately pitched Hunter and his family, going into detail about why he would be the right coach for Hunter, who wanted to play both sides of the ball. Sanders, an NFL Hall of Famer, had done it himself. “You want to play both sides of the ball? I’m definitely the coach that’s going to—you know, I’ve done it before—but you’re going to have to earn it,” Sanders said, according to Hunter. Hunter went on to say that Sanders not only helped develop him as a player but also truly changed his life. “I got too much respect for him,” Hunter added. “He came and got me to not go to Florida State and changed my mindset, changed the picture of everything. He really changed my life for real.” Travis Hunter Stands by Deion Sanders Amid Colorado Turmoil: ‘He Really Changed My Life’ Details: https://t.co/Bpes5GT3DM https://t.co/zlzYkUZLLm — Complex (@Complex) October 30, 2026 Sanders’ Colorado Future in Jeopardy While there’s been no indication that Colorado officials are willing to part ways with Sanders at this time, the team went 3-9 last season and appears on pace to finish with a similar record, if not worse, this year. That would mark the third time in Sanders’ four seasons as head coach that Colorado failed to become bowl eligible. ESPN’s Matt Barrie labeled Sanders’ Colorado tenure “as good as done.” Unless something drastically changes, that very well could be the only outcome of his time in Boulder. item.title: Jets’ Breece Hall shares inspiring message on social media
item.description: Vincent Carchietta-Imagn Images Jets’ Breece Hall shares inspiring message on social media appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Extra perseverance should be a requirement for any member of the modern-day New York Jets , but Breece Hall has faced other challenges besides frequent losing at the NFL level . The 25-year-old running back suffered a torn ACL and meniscus injury about midway through an impressive 2022 rookie campaign and is currently working his way back from a quadriceps issue that has already cost him four games this season. When facing such adversity, perspective is important. Hall has accomplished a great deal in his football career already, becoming a two-time All-American and Big 12 Offensive Player of the Year at Iowa State and accumulating 1,300-plus scrimmage yards with the Jets in each of the previous three years. He does not need to be defined by team success or personal accolades, however. The Wichita, Kansas native had plenty going against him, and yet, he is earning $29 million guaranteed with the Gang Green and enjoying life as one of the most well-rounded RBs in the league. While he nears his return, Hall is digging deep and offering words of encouragement to anyone who is enduring their challenges. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “To whoever needs to hear this: Through every high, every low, every setback, and every blessing, keep going and keep trusting in the Lord,” the 2022 second-round draft pick posted on X. “We may not always understand His timing or see the bigger picture, but His plan is always greater than ours. One day it’ll all make sense. Until then, keep your faith and trust His process.” This man is surely itching to get back on the field after a monthlong absence, but he is not letting that eagerness distract him from what is most important. Breece Hall has had some painful days before, and he is trying to spread some light to those who presently need it. The 5-foot-11, 217-pound back is in a good frame of mind ahead of Sunday afternoon’s game versus the visiting Las Vegas Raiders. Hall was a limited practice participant all week and is therefore considered questionable, but if he does play, the opposition will face off against a confident and trusting ball-carrier. item.title: Michael Malone Lands Five-Star Recruit with Help From North Carolina Legend
item.description: Michael Malone coaching North Carolina. Getty Michael Malone during an October 6th, 2026 game between North Carolina and USC. Getty Michael Jordan smiles during the NASCAR Cup Series GEICO 500 at Talladega Superspeedway on April 21, 2024 in Talladega, Alabama. Getty North Carolina head coach Michael Malone landed five-star recruit in DeMarcus Henry on Friday Henry’s commitment to the Tar Heels came over big time programs such as Arkansas, Louisville, Kentucky and UConn. According to Rivals, he’s ranked second among all players in the class of 2027. NEWS: 5⭐️ DeMarcus Henry has committed to North Carolina, he announced. The 6-foot-7 small forward and Charlotte native is the No. 2 overall player in the 2027 class. He picked UNC over Arkansas, Kentucky, and Louisville.https://t.co/ElidZwTDxn pic.twitter.com/Zho4VdPdur — Joe Tipton (@JoeTipton) October 30, 2026 It’s a massive pick up for Malone, who is hoping to establish a winning program on Chapel Hill. Henry made his decision following a phone call with one of North Carolina’s greatest players. Henry Brings Star Power to Michael Malone and UNC Getty Michael Malone during an October 6th, 2026 game between North Carolina and USC. At 6’7″ with a 6’11” wingspan, Henry’s athletic prowess jumps off the page. His defensive upside is obvious, with the ability to guard every position on the floor. That level of versatility gives Malone options when building the rest of his roster. Excellent rebounding skills and a knack for racking up blocks and steals should make the youngster an all-around contributor as well. On the other side of the ball, Henry has shown signs of improvement from long distance. He shot 38% from three-point range last season in the Nike Elite Youth Basketball League (EYBL). Overall, the forward notched 19.0 points per game on 52% shooting from the field. If there’s a critique with Henry’s skill set, he’s not the most refined playmaker. His early role with North Carolina might be as an elite three-and-D wing. Regardless, that’s still a terrific asset to have on campus. The Chandler, Arizona native comes from an athletic family as well. His father, Chris Henry, spent five seasons in the NFL with the Bengals . Older brother Chris Henry Jr. is a wide receiver currently enrolled at Ohio State . DeMarcus’ sister, Seini, is a basketball player at Ohio State. North Carolina Basketball Legend Helped Convince Henry Getty Michael Jordan smiles during the NASCAR Cup Series GEICO 500 at Talladega Superspeedway on April 21, 2024 in Talladega, Alabama. It’s no exaggeration to call this a game-changing pickup for UNC. The vibes around this team aren’t the best at the moment. North Carolina comes into the regular season unranked, a rarity for such a prestigious school. To make matters worse, the Tar Heels didn’t perform well during their preseason finale vs. Charlotte . By landing Henry, Malone gets to change the narrative around this program. This is North Carolina’s first addition for the class of 202

item.description: Bets predicted exact top-five men’s finishing order Organiser France Football has contacted police A series of suspicious bets that correctly predicted the exact top-five finishing order of this year’s Ballon d’Or and generated almost $200,000 (£149,000) in winnings is being investigated by the event’s organisers, France Football, who have also contacted the police. It has been alleged that 12 Polymarket accounts – an American cryptocurrency-based prediction market – placed the bets, with more than $264,000 wagered on the outcome before Monday’s ceremony. Their extraordinary accuracy has raised serious questions about a potential leak of confidential results before football’s most prestigious individual award. Harry Kane was crowned the winner at the ceremony at the London Palladium, finishing ahead of Kylian Mbappé, Lamine Yamal, Rodri and Lionel Messi. Remarkably, this was the exact order predicted by the group of accounts identified in French media outlet Upside’s investigation . Continue reading...

item.title: Arteta can take inspiration from George Graham to expunge painful Anfield memories
item.description: Arsenal have not won at Liverpool for 13 league games but Gunners’ win in 1989 remains one of club’s greatest nights Mikel Arteta used a Spanish word to describe what it felt like to be helpless at Anfield while playing for Everton in 2011: bajar . “It’s when a cyclist is going up and looks amazing, then in one kilometre he goes ‘boom’ and he’s struggling again,” he said in Amazon’s All or Nothing documentary. “The game was going well and then suddenly I could only see red shirts flying around. The game is passing all over me and I cannot react. I only had that feeling in my career once, and it was at Anfield.” Given Arteta’s record at Liverpool, Sunday’s showdown with his childhood friend Andoni Iraola – five days after Arsenal were dumped out of the Carabao Cup by Fleetwood – could be expected to fill him with dread. Arteta finally tasted victory there as a player with Arsenal in September 2012 , after five failed attempts in the Merseyside derby, but ended up spending the night in hospital with concussion after colliding with Jordan Henderson in an incident he has described as “the biggest fear of my life”. On 21 October, during a parliamentary committee meeting, politician Jeong Yeon-wook put a question to acting Korea Football Association (KFA) president Lee Yong-soo, that took a story out of the sports pages and into the national conversation. “It is said that recently, within the national team squad, players have been calling him not by his name but as ‘No 7’ or ‘that person’. item.title: An unmanageable club? Carrick the latest to suffer in Manchester United’s faded grandeur
item.description: Only Matt Busby and Alex Ferguson have truly succeeded in the Old Trafford hot seat with each casting uneasy shadows Should any football club fit the Great Man theory of history it is Manchester United. In the past 100 years, only Matt Busby and Alex Ferguson have knocked the club into shape. A pair of 20th-century Scotsmen, born 15 miles apart in Bellshill and Govan respectively, found the key. Otherwise, United has been a managerial dustbin, Michael Carrick the latest likely lobbed on the pile. Busby and Ferguson built the club around themselves, possessing the charisma to convince others that theirs was the path to follow. Carrick, an insider, a club man, is falling victim to the same isolation as his predecessors in failure . Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martínez going off-piste in TV interviews to depth charge Carrick were actually following club tradition. With glamour comes decadence, the faded grandeur that has so often chased a United manager out the door. Continue reading...

item.title: Mourinho’s plan comes together as Real Madrid relaunch with clásico statement | Sid Lowe
item.description: It was just like old times as José Mourinho ended a night at Camp Nou with a knee slide and three points José Mourinho had already done the por qu é? , the printout and the press conference no-show in under 100 days. Now he’s done a knee slide too, and in the perfect place: back where it all began and where it can all begin again. When Kylian Mbappé scored the first in the clásico on Sunday night, Real Madrid’s manager hardly moved, sitting in the shadow of the bench – but when the striker got the second to win it with time running out, that was different. Mourinho leapt into the light, throwing himself to the grass, the knees of a 63-year-old’s trousers muddy as a schoolboy’s, stuck his tongue out and pumped his fists. He does so love it when a plan comes together. To the right of him, the bench was emptying, subs joining the players in sprinting towards the south-west corner. As they leapt about, dodging the bottles thrown towards them from the end, way, way up in the furthest corner and stuck inside a glass box like a bunch of David Blaines, the small group of Madrid fans who had come were going mad. In the main stand, a thousand phones were raised. And 600 kilometres west, back in Boadilla, Thibaut Courtois was watching his teammates from the sofa at home, presumably wrapped in a blanket and cradling a cup of Lemsip. On the morning of the biggest game there is, he awoke with flu, forced to miss out. Continue reading...

item.title: The horse that ushered in Manchester United’s tragic arc | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: There’s plenty of blame to go around at Old Trafford. Like all downfalls it started with a seemingly small, unconnected moment Sign up for our free newsletter here And so here we are again, at that point as the nights draw in and Manchester United prepare to sack a manager . Autumn: season of mists, mellow fruitfulness and a crisis at Old Trafford. Sunday’s 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth , coming on the back of last week’s 4-1 reverse against Como, made clear what many had feared from the moment Michael Carrick was given the job on a permanent basis: that he isn’t up to it. But then, who could be? When you’ve burned through a long list of managers in 13 years, it’s perhaps worth considering whether the manager is really the problem. Could some blame perhaps go to the director of football, Jason Wilcox, or the chief executive, Omar Berrada, the people making the appointments? Or perhaps to Sir Jim Ratcliffe, the cost-cutting tax exile and minority shareholder with responsibility for sporting operations? Or to the Glazer family, who plunged the club into debt with a leveraged buyout in 2005 and have since made calamitous decision after calamitous decision, reducing the most successful club in English league history to a mid-table laughing stock with a roof that leaks symbolically ? item.description: Gunners edged north London derby while new United manager put the brakes on Manchester City’s winning start The penalty that allowed Arsenal to come from a goal behind to take the lead may have come with a healthy helping of luck, with the ball having come off Ella Morris’s raised arm as her teammate attempted to clear it, but it could prove to be the turning point Arsenal needed. “It’s been tough. We haven’t got the results we wanted,” penalty scorer Alessia Russo told the BBC afterwards. “This was an important win as far as north London derbies goes. It was really important and this was a great opportunity to try and turn it around.” It has taken seven games for the Gunners to secure their second league win of the season despite high hopes ahead of the new campaign and, while the result was a significant one, there is still a long way to go if Arsenal are to salvage anything from the most disappointing of starts. The performance against Tottenham was far from perfect and, in the first half in particular, sloppy and lacking fight. Tightening up their passing and harnessing the grit they found as they clung onto their lead towards the end of the match will be critical if they are to really kick on from this result. With just three minutes and the final reserves of energy remaining, a wonderful moment of skill from Jude Bellingham found Eduardo Camavinga and set them on one last run. Camavinga sprinted free, skilfully slipped Pau Cubarsí and pulled back for Kylian Mbappé to provide the finish, a little bit of history written. “The world that loves football will have stopped to watch this and they won’t have gone disappointed; this was two teams that played to win,” Mourinho said. It had been an intense, breathless ride, a proper battle, and it was his team who won it. Arriving right on time, Mbappé scored his second to make it 2-1, the Camp Nou falling quiet and their team given no time to react. item.title: Manchester City have been a joy to watch but they became detached from their roots | Philipp Lahm
item.description: City behaved much like other top clubs but their rule-breaking deserves to be punished. The Bundesliga, where members have a controlling stake, can show the way forward Do we have to reassess Manchester City now? In my columns, I have repeatedly engaged with this club and its key figures. Looking back at what I have written over the years, I believe it remains beyond question that the team have achieved greatness. I always loved watching them: they were a true unit on the pitch, a finely tuned orchestra. I would also write all over again that the conductor, Pep Guardiola, masters his craft like few others. I could recognise his teams even if they were wearing the wrong shirts and the game was broadcast in black and white – by the passes, the distances between the players and the intelligence of their interplay. It is no wonder Guardiola inspires others to become managers; look at Vincent Kompany, Mikel Arteta, Enzo Maresca, and perhaps some time Ilkay Gündogan and Rodri. Continue reading...

item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
